summary: Routing coalescer interaction produces sticky mixed-variant responses after low-weight canary slice
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Novello Health, enterprise) reports intermittent mixed-model outputs and degraded responses for long-lived chat sessions after we initiated a low-weight canary (5%) for gpt-redwood-v0.9. The symptoms started ~10 minutes after the canary was applied and persisted for some sessions even after canary weight was rolled back.

Impact:
- Several production users observed 'answer drift' and partial hallucinations compared to baseline v0.8 outputs.
- Affected tenant experienced a spike in user complaints; automated quality checks flagged ~12% regression on prompt suite for a cohort.
- Traffic is still served, but sessions are receiving inconsistent model variants mid-session which impacts end-user trust.

Environment:
- Hosted (Redwood API) production in us-east region.
- Tenant uses session affinity (sticky cookies) and model pinning to v0.8 for long-lived sessions.
- Canary: gpt-redwood-v0.9 rolled to 5% for gradual rollout window.

Observed behavior / hypothesis in short form:
Requests from the same session are sometimes routed to the canary variant despite the tenant pin. When the routing happens the edge/router returns a degraded fallback (v0.8-fallback) and the customer sees mixed outputs. We suspect an interaction between the new routing coalescer optimization (merges proxied inbound connections to reduce downstream fanout) and the session/pin scoping logic that allows stale affinity tokens to be applied to a coalesced request group, causing incorrect routing decisions and fallback activation.

Requested outcome:
- Restore strict tenant pinning/cohort affinity for Novello Health sessions.
- Confirm root cause and roll a safe fix that prevents coalescer from reusing affinity keys across pinning boundaries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a session for a tenant with model pin v0.8 and session cookie X-Session-ID=abc123
2) Start a low-weight canary for gpt-redwood-v0.9 (5%) in us-east region
3) From the same session, send 30 short chat requests at ~200ms intervals (to exercise coalescing path)
4) Observe intermittent routing to canary or fallback variant and mixed outputs in responses; confirm via route headers and model_name in tracing
Notes: Repro is timing-sensitive; best reproduced with a client that reuses a persistent HTTP/2 connection and sends small bursts.
logs: 2026-03-12T14:22:10Z edge-proxy INFO incoming request session=abc123 tenant=novello route=canary-check headers={cookie=...}
2026-03-12T14:22:10Z routing-coalescer DEBUG merged 6 inbound streams into group=grp-7f4a, affinity_key=tenant:novello:abc123
2026-03-12T14:22:10Z orchestrator WARN model-selection resolved_variant=v0.9 edge_pin_conflict=true fallback_invoked=v0.8-fallback
2026-03-12T14:22:11Z serving-runtime ERROR downstream 5xx from fallback-queue trace=tr-9a7b (partial response)
comments: Ana Martinez (reporter) - 2026-03-12: Customer reported degraded outputs at 14:20 UTC. Attached sample responses and session IDs.
Devon Li (assignee) - 2026-03-12: Investigating routing traces and coalescer logs. Initial glance shows coalescer grouping sessions across tenants when sessions reuse HTTP/2 multiplexed channels.
Marcus Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Hotfix option: we can disable coalescer for the tenant or globally until root cause is fixed. Preparing a targeted flip for Novello Health to mitigate impact.
Priya Singh (Applied ML) - 2026-03-13: Quality regression numbers align with customer's report for the affected cohort. Will provide prompt-level diffs once routing is stabilized.

Devon Li - 2026-03-13: Applied temporary mitigation: coalescer disabled for tenant novello in us-east at 03:40 UTC. Observed drop in mixed responses reported by customer. Keeping ticket open for RCA and permanent fix.
Ana Martinez - 2026-03-14: Customer confirmed improvement after mitigation but requested postmortem and timeline for permanent fix.
investigation: Checked routing trace ids: tr-9a7b, tr-9a9c, tr-9aaf showed coalescer group reuse across different session cookies when connections were reused.
Reproduced locally with a HTTP/2 client: when we enable coalescer + keepalive, group affinity_key generation omitted tenant-scoping in edge-proxy v2.1.3 build.

Race observed between pin-check (control plane snapshot) and coalescer group assignment when canary weight changes mid-burst: coalescer assigned group before latest pin snapshot was applied, causing inconsistent model resolution.

Edge-proxy header normalization was stripping a tenant-scoped header in some edge configs (side-effect of earlier header-sanitizer PR). This increases chance coalescer will not see tenant-scoped key and fallback to generic affinity.
Related config: routing-coalescer v1.4.0 introduced aggressive merge heuristics (merge_window=250ms) that exacerbate issue for short-burst sessions.

Hypothesis: coalescer was never designed to be pin-aware; it assumed per-connection affinity is sufficient. With canary weight changes and pin overrides, we need coalescer to include pin/token in group keys to guarantee per-tenant correctness.
mitigation: Temporarily disabled routing coalescer for tenant=novello in prod-us-east (done 2026-03-13 03:40 UTC). Customer reports no further mixed outputs after this change.
Added a temporary routing rule: force per-request pin-check bypassing coalescer grouping for any session with tenant-pin header until fix is released.
Alerted SRE and slated a rolling restart window to apply patched edge-proxy that preserves tenant-scoped headers for coalescer keying.
next_steps: 1) Implement coalescer keying change to include tenant-pin/session-pin in group key (engineering owner: Devon). Target patch by 2026-03-18.
2) Add unit/integration tests that simulate concurrent canary weight flips + coalescer merges (owner: QA).
3) Roll out patched coalescer behind feature flag; monitor model-selection divergence metric and client-reported quality metrics for 48 hours after rollout.
4) Produce postmortem summarizing root cause, mitigation, and concrete guardrails (owner: Ana). Due by 2026-03-20.
